samples.summary: The "one traversal" goal is only partly realized: `Doc.applyInlineStyle` deliberately ignores `range.tableCellRange` while its read counterpart `visitStyledRunsInRange` dispatches that shape to `visitCellRectangleSlices`. The routing burden is pushed back onto callers, and is now duplicated in two places (`view/editor.ts` `applyStyleImpl` line ~1022 and `view/text-editor.ts` `applyStyleToSelection`) — exactly the copy-the-dispatch pattern this change set out to eliminate. Dispatching `tableCellRange` inside `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (as the read already does) would make read/write symmetry structural instead of contractual, and the design doc's own 'One write path per editor' section documents the footgun rather than removing it.
samples.evidence: applyInlineStyle(range, style) { visitRangeSlices(...) } with doc comment "A `range.tableCellRange` is ignored here, as it always was"; range-runs.ts: `if (range.tableCellRange) { visitCellRectangleSlices(...); return; }`

samples.summary: The docs header/footer slim toolbar's B/I/U toggles got the *click* fix (decide from `getRangeStyleSummary`) but not the *pressed state* fix that the other two surfaces in this same change received (`TextFormatGroup` and the slides mobile bar now set `pressed={isStyleOn(summary.x)}`). The slim Toggles have no `pressed` prop at all, so their visual state is uncontrolled local React state and does not reflect the selection — the header/footer toolbar still cannot show "this range is bold", which is the same class of caret/range disagreement #715 is about.
samples.evidence: <Toggle size="sm" onPressedChange={toggleBold} className="h-7 w-7 cursor-pointer" aria-label="Bold"> — no `pressed` prop, while text-format-group.tsx:163 now uses pressed={isStyleOn(styleSummary?.bold)}

samples.summary: Design-doc placement: three new *model-layer* modules (`range-slices.ts`, `range-runs.ts`, `caret-style.ts`) that define how every read and write of inline style traverses a document are documented inside `docs-font-controls.md`, a feature doc whose stated subject is the font family/size pickers, line spacing and clear-formatting. This is a cross-cutting architecture change to the docs model; its canonical home is arguably `docs/design/docs/docs.md` (or `docs-named-styles.md` for the effective-style layering rule), with font-controls linking to it. The `docs/design/README.md` entry for docs-font-controls (line 53) was also not updated, so the index still describes the file as only the font-controls design and nothing in the index points at the new shared-traversal architecture.
samples.evidence: New sections 'The shared range traversal (model/range-slices.ts, model/range-runs.ts)', 'The shared caret walk (model/caret-style.ts)', 'One write path per editor' added to docs-font-controls.md; README.md:53 description unchanged.

Nested design docs are not link-checked by CI, so nothing else will catch the mismatch.

samples.summary: `applyStyleToCellRange` in `view/editor.ts` is now a one-line pass-through to `doc.applyInlineStyleToCells` with a doc comment longer than its body. Since the whole point of the change is to collapse duplicated indirection, the single caller (`applyStyleImpl`) could call `doc.applyInlineStyleToCells` directly, as `text-editor.ts` already does.

Possible scope creep beyond the toggle fix: `TextBoxEditorAPI.getSelectionStyle()` (and the collapsed-caret summary branch) now returns the *effective* style including named-style defaults, which changes what non-toggle consumers display for every editor built on `initializeTextBox` — notably the slides shape/text-box toolbars' color swatch and font-size/family pickers, which will now surface style-supplied values (e.g. heading-6's `#666666`) as if they were the run's own. The issue is about add-vs-remove toggles; widening the public caret read affects surfaces that only present or seed values. Worth confirming this is intended (the design doc asserts it is), and that no consumer stores the result.

Slides/text-box collapsed-caret toggles remain a dead end: `applyStyleImpl` returns immediately without a selection (no pending-style capture, unlike the full docs editor), so after this change the slides toolbar reports a correct effective pressed state at a caret but clicking B/I/U still does nothing. If #715's acceptance covers the slides text surfaces (the change touches the slides mobile toolbar), the caret half of the fix is missing there.
